manifest.name: Antigravity CLI
manifest.description: Launch the Google Antigravity CLI in Pragma with live status, approvals, questions, sub-agents, usage limits, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch the Google Antigravity CLI (agy) from the Pragma launcher with live status, command approvals, questions, sub-agent activity, quota usage limits, and session naming. The integration installs as a native Antigravity plugin and reports into Pragma's tab and sidebar, so Antigravity work in one worktree never hides progress in another.

manifest.name: Claude Code
manifest.description: Launch Claude Code in Pragma with live status, questions, usage limits, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Claude Code from the Pragma launcher and the integration reports live status, questions, approvals, usage limits, and session naming back to the app. Status lands on the tab, the sidebar, and agent alerts, so several Claude Code sessions stay readable side by side across worktrees.

manifest.name: Codex CLI
manifest.description: Launch Codex CLI in Pragma with live status, approvals, questions, usage limits, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Codex CLI from the Pragma launcher with live status, approvals, questions, usage limits, and session naming. Codex session events are bridged into Pragma's agent status store, so runs started here behave like any other agent tab.

manifest.name: Cursor Agent
manifest.description: Launch Cursor Agent in Pragma with live status, session naming, and account usage.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Cursor Agent from the Pragma launcher with live status, session naming, and account usage. The session reports into Pragma while it runs, so long Cursor jobs stay visible from any worktree without watching the terminal.

manifest.name: Grok Build
manifest.description: Launch Grok Build in Pragma with live status, questions, usage limits, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Grok Build from the Pragma launcher with live status, questions, usage limits, and session naming. Status and alerts arrive through the same agent-status plumbing as the built-in agents, so Grok sessions mix cleanly with everything else on the board.

manifest.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
manifest.description: Launch GitHub Copilot CLI in Pragma with status, approvals, questions, and quota reporting.
manifest.longDescription: Launch GitHub Copilot CLI from the Pragma launcher with status, approvals, questions, and quota reporting. Quota numbers surface next to the session, so you can see what a run is spending while it runs.

manifest.name: Junie CLI
manifest.description: Launch JetBrains Junie CLI in Pragma with live status, approvals, questions, usage limits, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch JetBrains Junie CLI from the Pragma launcher with live status, approvals, questions, usage limits, and session naming. The integration reports into Pragma's tab and sidebar, so Junie work in one worktree never hides progress in another.

manifest.name: Kimi Code CLI
manifest.description: Launch Kimi Code CLI in Pragma with live status, approvals, questions, subagents, and session naming.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Kimi Code CLI from the Pragma launcher with live status, questions, usage limits, subagents, and session naming. Subagent activity is reported alongside the main session, so nested work stays attributed to the tab that started it.

manifest.name: Oh My Pi
manifest.description: Launch Oh My Pi (omp) in Pragma with live status, sub-agent activity, session naming, and interjections.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Oh My Pi from the Pragma launcher with live status, sub-agent activity, session naming, resume, and interjections. omp sessions report into the same agent board as every other integration, and mid-run messages are delivered straight into the session.

manifest.name: OpenCode
manifest.description: Launch OpenCode in Pragma with streaming status, approvals, questions, and usage limits.
manifest.longDescription: Launch OpenCode from the Pragma launcher with streaming status, approvals, questions, and usage limits. The plugin wires OpenCode's event stream into Pragma, so a session started here reports progress live and can be answered from the tab or the agent board.

manifest.name: Pi
manifest.description: Launch Pi in Pragma with live status, session naming, and interjections.
manifest.longDescription: Launch Pi from the Pragma launcher with live status, session naming, and interjections. Interjections mean messages typed from Pragma land inside the running Pi session, so you can steer it without leaving the app.
